text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: `GPU-alloc-failed-prod` triggered for pool=gpu-v2 region=us-west-2 — 18 alerts in 2m. Auto-suppress threshold hit? https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD12345

alex (oncall): seeing the same. CPU looks fine, GPUs report CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED. Starting triage.

maria (sre): can you paste the top error from the node logs? looks like kv-cache eviction spikes + fragmentation.

alex (oncall): grabbing logs now.

alex (oncall): ```
[2026-03-15T12:10:02Z] gpu0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (code=2)
[2026-03-15T12:10:02Z] model-server: evicting kv-cache entry 0x7f... size=256MB
[2026-03-15T12:10:03Z] kvcache: fragmentation detected: free_chunks=3 total_free=1.2GB
```

noah (infra): interesting — there was a batch job that spiked sequence length around 12:05, could have amplified memory churn. I see a rolling deploy earlier too.

alex (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily scale up dedicated pool (add two nodes), 2) enable per-tenant soft-eviction throttle, 3) route heavy requests to fallback models (lower kv usage). Applying now.

maria (sre): +1 for draining affected nodes before rebooting. If fragmentation persists we should reboot the affected CUDA driver.

alex (oncall): running command to scale pool: `infractl pool scale gpu-v2 --add 2 --region us-west-2`

ops-bot: Command accepted, provisioning 2 nodes (expected ready ~3m).

alex (oncall): routing rules updated to send long-seq traffic to model=redwood-lite-v1: `routerctl route-add --match "seq_len>2048" --to redwood-lite-v1`

maria (sre): I'm enabling soft eviction throttle: `kvcachectl set throttle=0.6 --pool gpu-v2` — this reduces aggressive eviction churn.

cs-rebecca: any ETA on customer impact? Which customers hit errors?

alex (oncall): early telemetry: ~0.8% of requests in the last 5m returned 5xx CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED; customers using long-context batch jobs are affected (alpha-fin, convo-ai). Not a full outage.

maria (sre): node-level snapshot after scaling: fragmentation metrics improved on new nodes. Existing nodes still showing hotspots on gpu3,gpu5. Planning controlled reboot of gpu3 once drained.

alex (oncall): draining gpu3: `infractl node drain gpu3` — moving active sessions off. ETA 1m.

lee (next-oncall): I'll take handoff for the reboot and follow-up postmortem. Keep me in the loop.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert acknowledged by alex (oncall).

alex (oncall): drain complete, rebooting gpu3 now. Reboot command: `infractl node reboot gpu3 --force`

ops-bot: gpu3 reboot initiated.

noah (infra): after reboot, driver upgraded to 532.09 and CUDA reset. Observed immediate drop in alloc failures on that node.

maria (sre): good. I'll keep throttle in place for 30m and monitor fragmentation. Creating runbook note at https://confluence.example/runs/gpu-frag-2026-03-15

cs-rebecca: told alpha-fin and convo-ai that we saw transient 5xxs, mitigations in progress, and we're monitoring.

alex (oncall): handoff to lee: everything stable on scaled nodes, new nodes healthy, rate of CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED down to 0.05%. Leaving throttle=0.6 for now. Action items: (1) run full mem-frag analysis tomorrow (maria/noah), (2) add a preemptive throttle rule for long-seq bursts (maria), (3) customer follow-up note (cs-rebecca).

lee (next-oncall): acknowledged. I'll keep the runbook open and start the post-incident checklist. If errors reappear I'll escalate PD again.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: `GPU-alloc-failed-prod` status=resolved (auto) — alerts subsided.

alex (oncall): closing thread for now. I'll summarize in the postmortem draft. Thanks team :thumbsup:
